//: Extends the repo base, not `agents/tsconfig`. Inheriting a config out of node_modules meant the one package Vite actually bundles was the one package our own base config did not govern: it ran at ES2021 without `resolveJsonModule`, and a dependency bump could have changed its module settings. The Worker-shaped parts — DOM libs, workers-types, the React JSX runtime — are declared here because they are genuinely cf-backend's, and `verbatimModuleSyntax` moved to the base so this package keeps the check it already had while every other project gains it.
//files: `tests/workerd` is excluded because `tests/workerd/env.d.ts` augments `Cloudflare.Env` with the TEST worker's twelve probe bindings, and the agents SDK constrains its env generic to `Cloudflare.Env`, so compiling both surfaces together makes the production `Env` fail that constraint in every Agent class. `decorated-agent.test.ts` is the one workerd test that imports production Agent classes, so it needs the production `Env` and must not see the probe bindings. A `files` entry is not filtered by `exclude`, which is exactly the escape hatch this needs: one file, named, compiled against the surface it actually uses. It imports only `vitest`, `agents` and `./src`, so it needs nothing from the workerd project's types.
